title: fix: keep model catalogs loading during other session updates
body:
Related: #145679

The UI prerequisite #147973 is already merged. This branch retains its identical UI tree while the effective backend change is reviewed and validated.

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing a saved session's model list could fail with a retry error when another session changed, even if the selected session and its account were unchanged.

## User Impact

Saved-session catalogs remain usable during unrelated session updates. Changes to the selected session, its access, database owner, or model configuration still invalidate the pending response. No configuration, schema, migration, retention, or permission change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared session-list mutation counter was also fencing individual metadata reads. These reads now retain their selected row through the existing entry-cache and read-only database owners, release that lifetime in `finally`, and revalidate physical storage, routing, access, and configuration before responding. Exact reads do not load the full inventory, and per-model checks consume prepared in-memory facts. Existing catalog, authentication, and native-session ownership checks remain in place.

## Evidence

- The final combined candidate on the newer inventory-read base passes 247 focused Gateway/cache/replacement/child-session/prepared-query/Kysely/label-index/preflight/registry tests plus core and Gateway metadata types. Its four backend commits remain byte-identical after rebasing onto the final #147973 head. The complete UI tree matches that reviewed dependency, whose startup budget passes at 357,493 B versus the unchanged 361,938 B limit, with all translation values preserved.

- The real Gateway/local HTTP provider control passed before the fix; changing only another session's label during held discovery reproduced the failure. Both cases now pass.
- With 65 models, both cases preserve the complete ID/availability list and synthetic discovery account while doing one final physical-path check. This does not claim structural parity of every optional response field.
- 61 focused tests pass, covering selected-session mutation/reset, identical-row delete/recreate on both database connections, alias replacement, cold close/reopen, access/catalog ownership, native/draft selection, authentication replacement/config reload/dispatch, and existing entry-cache behavior. The final catalog-owner fixture rerun passes 19 tests.
- CI exposed one old metadata fixture that constructed a new config object on every read. A stable typed context fixes that fixture while preserving the production publication fence, saved pin, and exact neutral-scope assertions. The focused original case fails before the fixture correction; all 36 history/metadata tests and the gateway-other type graph pass afterward. P2 review of this test-only delta is scoped-clean. The final fixture reuses the helper’s existing stable config, removing redundant setup and fixing the file-length lint failure without weakening assertions.
- Inherited UI fixture failures are repaired in #147973 without changing assertions or thresholds. Its complete UI tree matches this branch, so its reviewed fixture and UI proof are reused. The new main-base metadata replacement and direct-child optimizations are also covered by the 247-test run.
- The full `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` gate passed for the production change, including all core/test typechecks, lint, dead-code scans and repository guards. The existing mixed `fullEntryKeys` payload test also passes. The final test-only directory-junction/owned-state fixture passes its three lifecycle cases and gateway-root typecheck on macOS; independent P2 review of that test-only delta is scoped-clean.

Source proof uses the authorized maintainer checkout, isolated test state, and a synthetic local provider. It uses no real provider credentials or live service changes.

<details>
<summary>Review and CI evidence</summary>

P2 autoreview reported one possible full-projection truncation. That finding was rejected after independent source checks: full, mixed, latest, uncached, and transactional reads return before the partial-cache expansion. Existing full/mixed projection tests protect their complete payloads and detachment. The original finding is retained in the local review record; this is not a scoped-clean automated verdict, and no actionable finding remains.

The first CI run exceeded the transformed-SDK ownership test’s 45-second limit. One diagnostic rerun on the same commit passed in 29.393 seconds with its 30-second child and 45-second test guards unchanged. The first job used Blacksmith; the rerun used GitHub-hosted runners under the existing policy. Local base/head comparisons showed no observed slowdown, while the exact original CI cause remains unproved.

</details>
